lines: 2026 Iran war 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis, Ships attacked during the 2026 Iran war Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps says that a supertanker carrying two million barrels of oil has sunk in the Strait of Hormuz after striking a mine. (Arab News)

Communal conflicts in Nigeria Religious violence in Nigeria The Nigerian Defence Headquarters announces that the Nigerian Army killed eight terrorists, arrested 22 additional terrorists, logistical personnel and their families, and rescued 125 kidnapping victims in various raids in the states of Adamawa, Bauchi, Yobe, and Borno between November 6 and 12. (The Vanguard)
Herder–farmer conflicts in Nigeria Three people are killed and several others are abducted in a cattle raid in Rabah, Sokoto State, Nigeria. (The Punch
Non-profit fanfiction repository website Archive of Our Own is restored to limited functionality 17 days after being targeted in a cybersecurity attack. (AP)

2026 Bangladesh garment workers protests Amid minimum wage protests by garment workers, 13 garment factories in Gazipur are shut indefinitely under the Bangladesh Labour Act, 2006 and over 50 remain closed in Savar and Ashulia, while 48 platoons of the Border Guard, Ansar, and Special Response Battalion deploy across industrial zones in Dhaka, Gazipur, and Narayanganj. (The Business Standard)
Twelve people are killed and 16 others are injured when a bus carrying gas refinery workers overturns in Ilam province, Iran. (Times of Israel)
Five people are injured, including three seriously, in a suspected gas explosion and fire at a Christmas market in Maredsous, Wallonia, Belgium. (Nederlandse Omroep Stichting in Dutch)

Australia–Philippines relations Australia and the Philippines sign a defence cooperation agreement in Manila, simplifying procedures for joint military exercises and expanding maritime surveillance, information sharing, training, and disaster response. (Reuters)

Estonia–Russia relations, Russian sabotage operations in Europe Estonia announces the closure of its three border crossings with Russia starting December 1 after eight suspects were detained over an attempted arson attack on drone manufacturer Threod Systems, which Estonian intelligence attributes to Russia's GRU. (CNN)

2026 Karak church shooting, Capital punishment in Jordan The Jordanian State Security Court sentences three men to death for an October 23 shooting at a Greek Orthodox church in Karak Governorate that killed nine people and injured 25 others. Two accomplices receive six-year prison sentences. (AFP via France 24)

2026 Cape Verdean presidential election Cape Verdeans vote to elect a president, where the main two candidates are the incumbent PAICV candidate José Maria Neves and the MpD candidate Joana Rosa. (AP)
2026 Gagauz general election Gagauzians in Moldova vote to elect a governor and 35 members of the People's Assembly. (Radio Moldova)

2026 European Tour In golf, Rory McIlroy equals Colin Montgomerie's record for the most Harry Vardon Trophies after winning his eighth Race to Dubai title, which McIlroy claimed after finishing second at the DP World Tour Championship. (AFP via France 24)

2026 Women's Rugby League World Cup, Australia–New Zealand sports rivalries In women's rugby league, Australia wins its fourth consecutive World Cup title after defeating New Zealand 34–10 in the final in Brisbane. (AFP via RFI)
